## Daily Report decision

Question: **When a new eBPF application generation reuses a pinned map, what proves that old bytes still have the schema and semantics expected by the new code?**

Current upstream libbpf revalidation shows automatic pinned-map reuse checks map type, key/value sizes, `max_entries`, flags, and `map_extra`; equal storage parameters can still hide structural or application-semantic incompatibility. Linux BTF exposes richer key/value type graphs, but BTF-local IDs are not cross-build semantic versions.

The report develops:
1. canonical BTF-derived structural fingerprints;
2. versioned map-state semantic contracts with migrate/reset/refuse outcomes;
3. shadow validation before the new generation receives write authority.

The broad reboot-persistence framing was rejected because bpffs pinning is not itself reboot-durable storage. A CO-RE semantic report and another host capability manifest were rejected as repetitions of September 18 and September 15/22 respectively.

## Acceptance

Before merge, require terminal-green final-head CI, complete diff/generated-output self-review, clean review threads, bilingual parity, and no private-source leakage. After squash merge, require successful production deployment for the exact merge SHA, generated/public English and Chinese verification including canonical/hreflang/Article metadata and sitemap inclusion, then exactly one compact top-level closeout comment on the merged PR.

The recurring operations schedule remains enabled and unchanged.
